item.title: Music on the Lawn: Paul Giess' Untethered — Sat Aug 15, 5:00 PM — LancasterHistory
item.description:
Music on the Lawn returns this summer with more fantastic local bands in James Buchanan’s backyard! This family- (and dog-) friendly event welcomes attendees to relax and enjoy an evening outdoors with live music. August’s concert features Untethered, featuring Paul Giess and Jazz Trio, Jam, a Philadelphia-based spontaneous composition and jazz collective led by Paul Giess with Lee Clarke, Timothy Ragsdale, and Mazae. We’ll also welcome the local ice cream shop, Splits & Giggles, who will serve delicious scoops while you enjoy the music!🍨
Registration is required. Walk-ins are welcome. LancasterHistory members get in free. Kids are free. Concerts are open to the public, and it’s a $10 donation for Adults. Attendees are encouraged to bring their own blanket or chair and pack a picnic if they like! Reminder: the Tanger Arboretum works really hard to beautify the grounds and keep all living things healthy. We ask that visitors treat the plants, flowers, and trees with extra kindness!

item.title: Covered Bridge Classic Ride — Sun Aug 16, 8:00 AM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup The Covered Bridge Classic is a premier Pennsylvania ride now in its 47th year. It offers beautiful routes of 100 mile, 66 mile, 54 mile, 31 mile, and 17 mile routes, in Lancaster County. Each route traverses through covered bridges and passes Amish farms. All routes cover rolling terrain with moderate climbing.
This one event funds all of our grants, free memberships and club expenses.
The cost of the ride is $50 and there are multiple start locations based on availability. To register, sign up at [https://coveredbridgeclassic.com/](https://coveredbridgeclassic.com/)
To volunteer, sign up at [https://www.lancasterbikeclub.net/content.aspx?page_id=2664&club_id=257148&actr=3](https://www.lancasterbikeclub.net/content.aspx?page_id=2664&club_id=257148&actr=3)

item.title: Evening Compline — Mon Aug 17, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Fall Open House at Perfect Pots — Sat Sep 5, 8:00 AM — Perfect Pots Greenhouse
item.description:
\Embrace the magic of the changing seasons at the Perfect Pots Fall Open House! Step into the Strasburg greenhouse to explore a vibrant selection of fall favorites—including bright celosia, colorful ornamental kale, and a huge variety of mums, all curated specifically for performance in container gardens. Guests can sip local apple cider and enjoy sweet seasonal treats while strolling through a greenhouse filled with inspiring autumn displays.
During the visit, attendees can join an expert designer for a Fall Garden Trends Tour to get fresh ideas and easy planting “recipes” (registration is suggested, but not required). Plus, visitors can take advantage of the Complimentary Design Service by dropping off mid-sized summer pots for the team to transform into fall masterpieces. Don’t forget to spin the wheel at checkout, where everyone wins discounts, garden goodies, and more! Perfect Pots looks forward to hosting a day of cozy seasonal vibes and creative inspiration for all.

item.title: All About Owls — Mon Oct 5, 4:00 PM — Lancaster
item.description:
Community, Presentation, Children
Learn about owls and the role they play in the ecosystem by dissecting real owl pellets with a Lancaster County Parks Naturalist.Owls swallow their prey whole, so they eventually have to spit what they can’t digest back up, packed into a tight bundle – an owl pellet. Owl pellets are valuable to scientists because they provide information about an owl’s diet and the types of prey available in its habitat. For this hands-on learning experience, participants will examine and identify the contents of their owl pellet – bones, fur, feathers, etc.Ages 5-10Space is limited | Registration is required
Source: Lancaster Libraries

item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
